# Heap allocation

Allocating, resizing and releasing blocks on the system heap.

<h2 id="alloc"><code>Alloc</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Alloc(size: uint) -> *var opaque
```

Allocates `size` uninitialized bytes.
Returns the base address, or null when the size overflows the platform bookkeeping or the system cannot satisfy
the request. A zero size is permitted, but the returned address is platform-dependent and must not be touched.
The allocation is owned by the caller until [`Free`](/docs/api/memory/allocation#free) releases it or [`Realloc`](/docs/api/memory/allocation#realloc) replaces it. The address is aligned
to at least 16 bytes on every supported target.
The bytes are uninitialized. Reading any byte before writing it, accessing beyond `size`, or using the address
after it is released is invalid.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Memory/Src/Alloc.rux#L29)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type   | Description                               |
| ------ | ------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `size` | `uint` | how many bytes to take; zero returns null |

**Returns**: the address of the allocation, or null when the system refused

<h2 id="free"><code>Free</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Free(ptr: *opaque)
```

Releases an allocation. A null pointer is accepted and does nothing.
A non-null `ptr` must be the live base address returned by [`Alloc`](/docs/api/memory/allocation#alloc) or [`Realloc`](/docs/api/memory/allocation#realloc). Every pointer into the block
becomes invalid immediately; releasing an interior, foreign, or already released address is invalid.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Memory/Src/Free.rux#L20)

**Parameters**

| Name  | Type      | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ----- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ptr` | `*opaque` | an address [`Alloc`](/docs/api/memory/allocation#alloc) or [`Realloc`](/docs/api/memory/allocation#realloc) returned, or null |

<h2 id="realloc"><code>Realloc</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Realloc(ptr: *opaque, size: uint) -> *var opaque
```

Resizes an allocation to `size` bytes, preserving the bytes that still fit.
A null `ptr` behaves as `Alloc(size)`. A zero size releases a non-null allocation and returns null. On failure,
returns null and leaves the original allocation valid; on success, the original address is invalid even when the
returned address has the same numeric value.
A non-null `ptr` must be the live base address returned by [`Alloc`](/docs/api/memory/allocation#alloc) or an earlier `Realloc`. Interior, released,
or foreign addresses are invalid. Bytes added beyond the old size are uninitialized.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Memory/Src/Realloc.rux#L23)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type      | Description                                     |
| ------ | --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `ptr`  | `*opaque` | the allocation to resize, or null to allocate   |
| `size` | `uint`    | the wanted size; zero releases and returns null |

**Returns**: the address of the resized allocation, or null on failure
